bullets: An underwater frame is built around backscatter management before composition — once that priority is internalized, the downstream decisions get easier, and ignoring it means rebuilding from scratch a year later.
Strobe positioning at 45 degrees is the starting point rather than the destination; it is a default to adjust from, not a fixed rule.
Adobe Lightroom underwater work is half about white balance and half about removing magenta, so color correction means handling both problems rather than treating white balance alone as the fix.
The frame should reward the eye in the first three seconds — the framing matters because it reveals which trade-offs are being made.
Strobe lighting trade-offs cut across every other underwater imaging decision, linking backscatter, color, and composition rather than standing as a separate concern.
Outside of Capture One-class tooling, the failure mode is harder to spot; the second-order effects of these choices are the part most people miss.
Picking one idea and running it for two weeks is the recommended way to start, with everything beyond that treated as iteration.
